title: A simple and robust HPLC method to analyze lutein in wheat
author: Wu, Li, et al.

steps.title: Prepare and degas mobile phases
steps.instruction: Mix acetonitrile (A), methanol (B), and n‑hexane (C) to obtain the initial composition of 76 % A, 21.5 % B, and 2.5 % C; sonicate the mixture for 20 min to degas.

steps.title: Configure HPLC system
steps.instruction: Install an InfinityLab Poroshell 120EC‑C18 column (4.6 × 150 mm, 4 µm) on an Agilent 1260 HPLC; set injector temperature to 4 °C, column oven to 25 °C, flow rate to 1 mL min⁻¹, injection volume to 50 µL, and detector wavelength to 450 nm.

steps.title: Program gradient elution
steps.instruction: Program the gradient as follows: start at 76 % A / 21.5 % B / 2.5 % C; linearly decrease A from 76 % to 70 % and B from 21.5 % to 20 % between 20 min and 22 min; then from 28 min to 30 min increase A back to 76 % and B back to 21.5 % (C remains at 2.5 %).

steps.title: Prepare lutein standard dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare five different dilutions of lutein standard covering the linear range 1.0–10.0 µg mL⁻¹ (e.g., 1, 3, 5, 7, 10 µg mL⁻¹) for calibration and generate a five‑point calibration curve; also prepare spiking solutions of known concentrations for accuracy assessment.

steps.title: Run standards and samples
steps.instruction: Inject each standard dilution and wheat extract under the programmed conditions; record the retention time (expected 3.23 min) and peak area at 450 nm; construct the calibration regression line (R² = 0.999) and calculate sample lutein concentrations using the external standard curve.

steps.title: Validate method performance
steps.instruction: Confirm that sample retention time matches the standard (3.23 min); assess repeatability by injecting the five standards repeatedly and verifying single, stable peaks; perform recovery experiments on four wheat genotypes by spiking known lutein amounts and calculate recoveries (average > 95 %); compute reproducibility as relative standard deviation (RSD = 3.25–4.38 %); determine LOD and LOQ from signal‑to‑noise ratios (LOD = 812 ng mL⁻¹, LOQ = 1242 ng mL⁻¹).

description: According to the above chromatographic conditions, the retention time of standard sample was 3.23 min, and the retention time of lutein in wheat sample was 3.23 min, indicating that the retention time of wheat sample was consistent with that of standard sample, and the same substance was detected (Fig. 1. A B). Five different concentrations of standard solution were used to make the standard curve, and the repeatability of the determination method of wheat lutein under the determined elution conditions was verified (Fig. 1. C). The five standard curves were single peak at 450 nm with good retention time, repeatability and relatively stable, which indicated that the method for the determination of lutein was reliable.Fig. 1HPLC chromatogram of lutein from standard(A),wheat samples(B),lutein with different concentrations(C)Fig 1 To test the robustness of extraction and analytical method, recovery experiments were investigated.
